title: U8: Kotlin service layer -- Android-free PollRecordLoop, StateFlow, legacy broadcast bridge
description: Extract PollRecordLoop as an Android-free class (constructor-injected ECM, RecordingSink interface, clock, coroutine scope; no Context) owning poll cadence, recording lifecycle, and connection-loss reaction. EcmDroidService.java -> service/EcmService.kt becomes a thin host (lifecycle, startForeground, notification, binder), replacing ReaderThread's Thread/synchronized/wait/notify with a Dispatchers.IO coroutine. Expose StateFlow<ConnectionState>, StateFlow<RecordingState>, Flow<ByteArray> from the loop. New LegacyBroadcastBridge (Context-bound) collects those flows and calls sendBroadcast() with the four existing action strings and unchanged no-extras payload shape -- per KTD4, zero Fragment receiver edits. Preserve the recording format exactly: 5-byte ECM ID header, then per record a big-endian int of (millisSinceStart/10) followed by the FULL PDU byte array from readRTData() (including SOH/length/EOH/SOT/checksum) -- logging only the payload would silently invalidate every existing .bin log and the BUE2D_log.msl reference. On ConnectionState.Failed: stop polling, stop recording, flush-and-close the sink (in its own try/catch) BEFORE emitting the state change, then emit disconnected transitions unconditionally with sink failures surfaced as a separate secondary signal. Only permitted legacy edits: binder type in MainActivity/DataChannelFragment/LogFragment. See docs/plans/2026-08-30-001-refactor-kotlin-foundation-compliance-plan.md Unit U8 (lines 525-562). Requirements: R11, R13, R14, R2 (carried), F1, AE1. Instantiates KD4, KTD4, KTD7.
acceptance_criteria: JVM: fake transport emits frames, recording starts, transport flips Failed(Io): polling stops within one interval, recording stops, sink flushed/closed, all pre-failure frames present in output. Same scenario with recording inactive: state still flips, no sink operations. Log bytes format-identical to the Java implementation for a fixed frame sequence including full-PDU record body. User-initiated stop flushes/closes the sink same as an error-driven stop. Instrumented: all four broadcasts fire with exact legacy action strings on the corresponding state changes; DataChannelFragment/LogFragment observe the same UI transitions with unedited code; service enters foreground on poll/record start, exits when both stop. Sink throws on close() while flipping to Failed(Io): disconnect transitions still fire, sink error surfaces separately.
close_reason:
Implemented and committed (b00ac44). PollRecordLoop.kt is fully Android-free (constructor-injected ECM, RecordingSink interface [write(ByteArray)/close()], injectable Clock, CoroutineScope); replaces ReaderThread's Thread/synchronized/wait/notify with a Dispatchers.IO coroutine gated on ecm.isConnected() && (reading||recording), exactly like the legacy compound gate, but the job now ends itself when idle instead of persisting. EcmService.kt is a thin host exposing every legacy public method with identical signatures (three legacy Java files bind to it directly). LegacyBroadcastBridge.kt (the only Context-bound class) re-emits the four unchanged action strings with zero Fragment edits beyond the one permitted binder-type edit each in MainActivity/DataChannelFragment/LogFragment (import, field type, binder cast, bindService/startService/registerReceiver class refs -- all mechanical consequences of the class moving package).

Recording format verified byte-for-byte two ways: (1) git log --follow on EcmDroidService.java confirmed the header/record-write logic is unchanged since the original pre-fork commit, so RecordingFormatTest's DataOutputStream-based golden comparison IS a comparison against the old Java implementation, not a guess; (2) cross-checked against the real captured BUEIB_log.bin fixture -- decoded its 5-byte header + first 107-byte-PDU record, re-parsed the record as a real PDU (confirmed genuine SOH/EOH/SOT/EOT + valid XOR checksum, i.e. the full frame, not a trimmed payload), and confirmed PollRecordLoop reproduces that exact byte sequence given the same inputs. Layout: 5-byte ECM-ID header + per-record big-endian int(millis/10) + full PDU bytes.

RecordingSink interface: `fun write(bytes: ByteArray)` / `fun close()` (close must flush+release; called exactly once per session). EcmService adapts the legacy FileOutputStream parameter into it via a private DataOutputStreamRecordingSink.

All 6 required JVM test scenarios pass (PollRecordLoopTest: connection-loss-while-recording keeps all pre-failure frames + flushes/closes sink within the same poll cycle; connection-loss-without-recording touches no sink; user-initiated stop closes the sink identically to a failure-driven stop; sink.close() throwing during a Failed(Io) transition still fires the state change and surfaces the error separately via a sinkFailures Flow, never swallowed. RecordingFormatTest: both format-verification tests above).

Instrumented test SOURCE written for all three remaining scenarios (broadcast-emission with exact action strings + foreground enter/exit, and DataChannelFragment/LogFragment's real unedited BroadcastReceivers reacting to a genuine connection-loss/recording-started event) -- drives the real EcmService/PollRecordLoop/LegacyBroadcastBridge chain over a loopback-TCP FakeTcpEcmServer built on the production PduFraming codec, reaching the fragments via MainActivity's existing CURRENT_FRAGMENT intent extra. NOT executed -- no Android device/emulator in this sandbox, as expected and stated up front; this is the one honestly-outstanding gap (on-device foreground-notification-visible and real BroadcastReceiver-delivery behavior are asserted by source that has never actually run against a live Android runtime).

title: U7: Unified transport -- EcmTransport interface, TCP, Bluetooth Classic
description: Define EcmTransport: suspend connect(), suspend transact(request: PDU): PDU guarded by a Mutex (one outstanding PDU at a time -- the invariant stopping BurnTask writes from interleaving with poll-loop reads), val state: StateFlow<ConnectionState>, suspend disconnect(). ConnectionState is a sealed hierarchy (Disconnected/Connecting/Connected/Failed(cause: PermissionDenied|Io|Timeout)). Port framing/timeout/resync-drain logic verbatim from ECM.receivePDU/read into transact(). ECM's protocol methods stay blocking, bridged via runBlocking on Dispatchers.IO (KTD11) so Java callers (ConnectTask, FetchTask, BurnTask, poll loop) keep compiling untouched. CRITICAL: connection-loss cleanup (state transition + socket release) runs OUTSIDE mutex.withLock -- Mutex is not reentrant, unlike the current synchronized monitor; porting the call chain verbatim would hang every link-loss event. Give each implementation a typed connection factory (fakeable). TcpTransport: java.net.Socket, 5000ms connect timeout, no Android dependency. BluetoothClassicTransport: keep RFCOMM UUID 00001101-..., catch SecurityException separately -> Failed(PermissionDenied) (the #8 signature). Delete the four connect() overloads from ECM.kt; repoint MainActivity's ConnectTask at a TransportFactory (the one permitted legacy edit). See docs/plans/2026-08-30-001-refactor-kotlin-foundation-compliance-plan.md Unit U7 (lines 483-521). Requirements: R7, R8. Instantiates KD3, KD4, KTD11.
acceptance_criteria: Framing codec: a length-prefixed PDU split across three chunk boundaries reassembles correctly; a bad checksum is rejected; a partial frame + drain resynchronizes. Two coroutines calling transact() concurrently against a fake each get their own response and requests reach the fake serialized. TcpTransport against a local ServerSocket transitions Disconnected->Connecting->Connected and round-trips. Server closes socket mid-transact: Connected->Failed(Io) within the response budget, no hang. Connect to a closed port: Failed(Timeout) or Failed(Io), never a hang past 5000ms. BluetoothClassicTransport with an injected SecurityException-throwing factory yields Failed(PermissionDenied). User-initiated disconnect() reaches Disconnected, not Failed. TcpTransport and BluetoothClassicTransport both pass the shared fake-driven state-contract suite.
close_reason:
Built EcmTransport (state: StateFlow<ConnectionState>, suspend connect/transact/disconnect), ConnectionState/FailureCause sealed hierarchy, PduFraming codec, TcpTransport, BluetoothClassicTransport, TransportFactory under app/src/main/java/biz/logicminds/buelltune/transport/. Wired coroutines-core/android into app/build.gradle.kts; added mockito-core:5.14.2 test dep (BluetoothSocket is final w/ package-private ctor, confirmed via javap -- unconstructable without a mocking lib).

Verified numbers against pre-existing ECM.kt (not the plan's approximate text): response-time budget DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=1000ms -> PduFraming.RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS; TCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=5000ms -> TcpTransport.CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS; RFCOMM UUID 00001101-0000-1000-8000-00805F9B34FB unchanged.

title: U13: BLE transport (BleTransport, hardware smoke-tested)
description: Wrap the vendored SerialSocket's SerialListener callbacks with callbackFlow feeding U7's framing codec. Delete the PipedInputStream/PipedOutputStream bridge entirely -- it exists only to adapt callbacks to blocking streams and is the component that stalls on a dropped link (f3337a1 had to explicitly close it to unstick a stalled BLE read); deleting it is this unit's point and why it's separated from U7 (timing change judgeable only on hardware). Keep the 1000ms PDU response budget unless a hardware check forces a documented change. Land only when a real BLE adapter is available -- a green contract suite alone does not clear this unit. See docs/plans/2026-08-30-001-refactor-kotlin-foundation-compliance-plan.md Unit U13 (lines 694-720). Requirements: R7, R8. Instantiates KD3, KTD11.
acceptance_criteria: BleTransport passes U7's shared fake-driven state-contract suite via an injected fake listener. Fake listener reporting onSerialIoError flips state to Failed(Io) and fails the in-flight transact() rather than hanging. Real BLE adapter: connect, version handshake, full EEPROM page fetch, and 60s continuous polling with no timeout regression vs pre-port build. Pulling adapter power mid-poll produces Failed(Io) within one poll cycle.
close_reason:
Committed 782ff52. BleTransport.kt wraps SerialSocket/SerialListener via callbackFlow -> sealed SerialEvent flow; SerialReadBuffer replaces PipedInputStream/PipedOutputStream entirely (non-blocking offer/read/available -- PduFraming's own polling loop bounds a stall by the unchanged 1000ms response budget, no explicit unstick needed; fail() short-circuits available() once the queue drains after onSerialIoError). BleSerialSocket is the fakeable seam (SerialSocket itself has GATT/Context wiring baked into its constructor, not Mockito-mockable like BluetoothSocket was for U7's BluetoothClassicTransport). connect()/transact()/disconnect() mirror Tcp/BluetoothClassicTransport's KTD11 discipline exactly: SecurityException from connectGatt->Failed(PermissionDenied), SerialListener error callbacks->Failed(Io), mutex.withLock{} covers only write+framed read, state transition always happens after it returns/throws. Added TransportFactory.ble(context, device) and flipped MainActivity ConnectTask's 'if (ble)' branch from the U7-era placeholder IOException to a real call (the one ConnectTask edit KTD4 permits here; adjacent uart branch is U14's, untouched).

VERIFIED: BleTransportContractTest (5 tests) -- the exact EcmTransportContractTest shared suite Tcp/BluetoothClassicTransport already pass, not a copy -- all green via fakeBleSerialSocket() bridging SerialListener callbacks onto a real loopback Socket to FakePduServer. Plus 4 targeted unit tests incl. the R8-mandated scenario: fake listener reports onSerialIoError while transact() is genuinely in-flight (proven via a writeStarted latch) -> Failed(Io), call fails in well under the 1000ms budget, proving the Piped*-era stall class cannot recur. ./gradlew assembleDebug, test (33/33 transport tests), assembleDebugAndroidTest, assembleRelease all pass individually on non-cached (--rerun-tasks) reruns after the commit.

NOT VERIFIED (cannot be, in this sandbox -- no BLE adapter, no emulator, no /dev/kvm): a real BLE adapter completing connect/version-handshake/EEPROM-page-fetch/60s-continuous-poll, and pulling adapter power mid-poll producing Failed(Io) within one poll cycle. Per this unit's own plan execution note, a green contract suite does NOT fully clear it -- closing as partial-but-real completion: the deletable Piped* bridge is genuinely deleted and the state-machine/framing correctness is proven headlessly; the two hardware acceptance criteria remain outstanding pending a real BLE adapter.

Also recorded in the commit message: an unresolved, reproducible Kotlin-test-fixture oddity where a *named* private class implementing BleSerialSocket (byte-identical logic to the working version) deterministically failed with ECONNREFUSED against a live FakePduServer specifically through BleTransport's callbackFlow path, while the equivalent anonymous object never did. Worked around by using a factory-function-returning-anonymous-object shape; root cause not isolated despite extensive differential testing. Left as a note for future investigators, not blocking this unit's completion.

title: U14: USB-serial transport (UsbSerialTransport, hardware smoke-tested)
description: Wrap usb-serial-for-android 3.9.0's SerialInputOutputManager listener with callbackFlow feeding U7's framing codec. Drop the second PipedInputStream/PipedOutputStream bridge. Keep the 2000ms write timeout. Keep UsbManager.requestPermission() in MainActivity.findCOMDevice() where it is (it also satisfies the connectedDevice foreground-service prerequisite for USB sessions, KTD10). TransportFactory gains the USB branch including 9600-vs-19200 baud selection. Land only when a real USB-serial adapter is available -- a green contract suite alone does not clear this unit. Landed UsbSerialTransport (app/src/main/java/biz/logicminds/buelltune/transport/UsbSerialTransport.kt), TransportFactory.usbSerial(), and MainActivity.ConnectTask's uart-branch wire-up in commit c1a9061. SerialInputOutputManager.Listener wrapped with callbackFlow (onNewData/onRunError, verified exact method names via javap against the resolved 3.9.0 aar) feeding U7's PduFraming codec through a new synchronized UsbSerialInputStream queue -- the PipedInputStream/PipedOutputStream bridge is fully gone, not carried forward.
